scope.summary: Introduce the ADR-0531 oya-bot-autofix app skeleton with a dry-run renderer for one oya-ci-gate-contract remediation and a PROPOSE-only policy that denies merge and gate-bypass actions.
explicit_non_claims: No bot merge capability, branch-protection bypass, or oya-ci-required bypass is introduced.
No webhook delivery, scheduled burn-down, third-party pack registration, or GitHub PR creation runtime is introduced in this slice.
The dry-run renderer applies a single described remediation in memory only and prints a reviewable diff; it does not write repository files.

facets.F1_correctness: render_dry_run accepts an oya-ci-gate-contract Remediation::AutoFix, validates the described byte range, and returns a deterministic diff containing the proposed added license line for the fixture remediation.
facets.F2_tests: Cargo and Buck2 tests cover dry-run diff rendering, no-write safety envelope, allowed dry-run/propose actions, and denial of merge and gate-bypass actions.
facets.F3_maintainability: The bot skeleton is isolated in tools/oya-bot-autofix-app with a narrow library API and a thin CLI wrapper; delivery/runtime expansion remains outside this slice.
facets.F4_compatibility: Workspace inclusion uses the existing tools/oya-* glob; Cargo.lock adds only the new workspace package; the capability registry maps the tool to build/ and a catalog row records preview status.
facets.F5_security: The crate forbids unsafe code, dry-run reports writes_performed=false, and BotPolicy::propose_only rejects MergePullRequest and BypassGates by construction.
facets.F6_privacy: The skeleton processes generic source text from stdin or test fixtures only and carries no tenant, customer, or personal data.
facets.F7_operability: Cargo and Buck2 targets are present for library, binary, and the dry-run integration test; the CLI can render a dry-run diff and exits non-zero for forbidden merge commands.
facets.F8_performance: The renderer performs a bounded in-memory string replacement over one described remediation; no service loop or background runtime is introduced.
facets.F9_compliance: ADR-0531 safety invariants are preserved for this atomic slice: dry-run/preview exists, proposal remains reviewable data, and merge/bypass authority is denied.
facets.F10_reversibility: The change is an isolated new tool crate plus registry/catalog/evidence metadata and can be reverted without migrations or deployed state changes.
facets.F11_observability: The evidence packet records task, branch, changed files, verification commands, safety non-claims, and remaining review/PR governance gaps.
facets.F13_migration: This is the first oya-bot-autofix skeleton after REMED-001; broader apply/propose PR delivery, HMAC webhook integration, and scheduled burn-down remain future serialized remediation cards.
facets.A1_naming_adherence: The package name oya-bot-autofix-app follows the tools/ app naming convention and ADR-0531's canonical oya-bot-autofix name.
facets.A2_documentation_adherence: The crate docs cite ADR-0531 and state the PROPOSE-only, no merge/bypass scope.
facets.A3_structure_adherence: Cargo.toml, BUCK, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, and tests/dry_run.rs follow neighboring Rust tool crate conventions.
facets.A4_architecture_adherence: The dry-run path consumes described remediation data from oya-ci-gate-contract and keeps privileged delivery/merge authority out of the skeleton.
facets.A5_dependency_adherence: No new third-party dependency is introduced; the crate depends only on the local oya-ci-gate-contract crate.
facets.A6_schema_adherence: No new machine-readable schema is introduced; the catalog YAML and capability-registry row follow existing registry shapes.
facets.A7_algorithm_adherence: Byte ranges are checked for bounds and UTF-8 boundaries before an in-memory replacement is rendered into a deterministic whole-file unified diff.
